summary: Iteration 5 — Scheduler (APScheduler) + Calendar (FullCalendar) feature pass. 19/20 backend pytest cases PASS (1 minor FAIL: GET /api/calendar/events 500s on unparseable date params due to naive/aware datetime comparison). All frontend checks PASS (11/11): admin/coach/parent sidebars contain 'Calendar' nav (data-testid='nav--calendar'); /calendar route renders FullCalendar grid; admin sees 4+ weekly-expanded events painted with skill-level colors; clicking an event opens event-dialog with skill_level/coach/location/capacity/monthly_price; week/day/month view buttons work; /admin/settings → 'Automation' tab opens scheduler-panel showing next_run_time for both jobs (2026-06-01 09:00 invoices, 2026-06-05 09:00 reminders), target period 2026-06, and 'Run now' buttons fire endpoints without errors. APScheduler running:true visible at /api/scheduler/status; both crons registered with valid ISO next_run_time. /api/scheduler/run-monthly-invoices for 2099-02 is idempotent (created=N first call, created=0 second). /api/scheduler/run-dues-reminders returned 200 with sent/failed/skipped counts (sandbox mode → skipped, no 5xx). Recurrence math correct: events for a Wed-only session only land on Wednesdays within session.start_date..end_date window. Required-param 422 returned when start/end missing. minor.issue: Returns 500 (TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes) when fallback path triggers. _parse_date returns naive datetime via datetime.strptime, while the default fallback in calendar_routes.py:112 uses datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(day=1) which is aware. The mismatch surfaces at _expand_session line 69 `max(sess_start, range_start)`. Fix: make _parse_date return tz-aware datetimes (or strip tz from the fallback). FullCalendar always sends valid ISO so prod users won't hit this, but a malformed query param from any client crashes the endpoint with 500 instead of falling back to defaults as the route comment promises.

routers/calendar_routes.py:_parse_date — returns NAIVE datetime; fallback at line 112 uses datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(day=1) which is AWARE. rca_of_the_issue: calendar 500 RCA: _parse_date in /app/backend/routers/calendar_routes.py:35-43 returns a tz-naive datetime (datetime.strptime). When the input fails to parse, the fallback at line 112 uses datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(day=1) which is tz-AWARE. Inside _expand_session (line 69), `max(sess_start, range_start)` raises TypeError because sess_start (parsed from session.start_date as naive) cannot be compared to the aware range_start. Reproduction: GET /api/calendar/events?start=not-a-date&end=also-bad with admin cookies → 500 Internal Server Error. Mitigation: change line 40 to `return datetime.strptime(...).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` so all parsed datetimes are tz-aware; the fallback already is. Alternatively normalize the fallback to naive. Recommend tz-aware everywhere for clarity.
